messages:
maria: Quick heads up — running the new FlashAttention-v2 build against the paged-KV runtime shows a tail-latency regression when mixed batch sizes (16/64/256) hit hot paths. Not consistent, but repeatable on the nightly cluster :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the numbers and the command you ran?

maria: Sure, minimal repro run:```./perf-bench --model=gpt-medium --attn=flashv2 --kv-mode=paged --batch-distribution=16:40,64:40,256:20 --seq=1024 --iters=200```

maria: Output snip:```p50: 48ms p95: 132ms p99: 410ms (prev: p99 340ms) throughput: -6%```

ash: Interesting. Do we know if the regression is due to kernel choice or KV pager contention? FlashV2 swaps in a few new kernels that assume dense KV memory locality. Paged KV breaks that locality.

devon: I profiled the NVTX regions quickly. When p99 spikes, GPU stalls on memory copies right after the attn kernel returns — looks like scatter/gather for the block table refill.

perf-bot: nightly-ci/flashv2-pagedkv #42: regressed 12.3% p99 vs baseline. Logs uploaded to https://ci.internal/reports/42

sam: Hypothesis: kernel selector favors flashv2 fused-block kernel for medium seqs because it has better noop cycles when dense. But when KV pages miss, the ensuing async page fetches make the fused kernel hold the SMs longer, increasing tail. We might need a heuristic: if kv_paged==true and frac_large_batches < 0.5 then prefer the streaming/fallback kernel.

ash: Agreed. Also alloc strategy for the block-table matters — current allocator does per-request small allocations which fragments device memory and increases page faults. We should either use a slab allocator or pre-allocate per-shard block table arenas.

devon: I prototyped a slab-mode flag in the pager:```pager.config { mode: slab_prealloc, slab_size_mb: 64, frag_threshold_pct: 15 }``` With that enabled, initial runs look promising: p99 improved from 410ms -> 360ms but still above baseline.

maria: Good delta. Any idea on batching heuristic? Our current batcher mixes based on token-age only. If a request is likely to cause a page miss (no KV hint) we should bias it to smaller micro-batches so we don't amplify the miss.

sam: Could add a micro-heuristic: tag requests with kv_cache_hint in the router (hot/warm/cold); then batcher applies max_batch_size = lookup_table[kv_hint]. Example mapping: hot->512, warm->128, cold->32. Keeps hot steady and isolates cold misses.

ash: Implementation detail: need a cheap estimator for kv_cache_hint at entry. We can use recent-prefix-hits % over the session or access frequency from traces. No heavy lookups.

devon: Also seeing block-table allocation thrash under concurrent small batches. If we prefetch block-table entries on a per-shard worker thread we can hide page fetch latency and keep kernels streaming. But prefetch policy mustn't pollute cache. Maybe prefetch only when request likely to continue (user-level ribbon ticket).

maria: Actionables: 1) sam will add kernel-selector flag to prefer streaming kernel when paged-KV is enabled (owner: sam, PR spike by EOD). 2) devon will push slab allocator toggle and run perf matrix (owner: devon, results tomorrow). 3) ash will prototype kv_hint tagging in router (owner: ash). I'll run a full nightly once changes land. :rocket:

infra-bot: Created tickets: RUNTIME-907 (kernel-selector heuristic), RUNTIME-908 (pager-slab-mode), RUNTIME-909 (kv-hint-router).

maria: Thanks. If anyone wants to pair on the profiler traces, ping me — I captured the NVTX timeline and a small repro environment.

sam: I'll take the kernel-selector PR and add a canary on dedicated pool so we don't roll the change to all customers at once.

maria: Perfect. I'll update the issue with the repro artifacts and the perf patch notes.
